step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified system entry point: 'Users' (represented as UserConsumerWeb) uploading documents to the Turnitin web application.
2. Ingestion pipeline: SNS receives upload notifications and pushes messages into an SQS queue for buffering up to 2 million papers daily.
3. Rules and Processing: An Orchestrator Lambda (written in Java) reads from SQS to validate document eligibility based on length and language rules. Valid papers are handed off to a Processing Lambda (written in Python) which strips out non-prose elements (headers, footers) and creates sentence sliding windows.
4. Inference: Processing Lambda sends 10 sentence segments in parallel to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint running on EC2 for AI inference score calculation, then aggregates sentence scores.
5. Persistence and Retrieval: The Processing Lambda passes aggregated scores back to the Orchestrator Lambda, which writes the sentence and document scores into DynamoDB. A Micro Front End (MFE) component queries the Orchestrator Lambda to fetch document evaluation scores stored in DynamoDB for instructor display.

graph.name: Turnitin Generative AI Academic Integrity Architecture
graph.notes: Turnitin processes up to 2 million papers per day using an event-driven architecture with AWS Lambda, SageMaker on EC2, and DynamoDB across three AWS regions (US, Europe, Asia Pacific).

nodes.name: Users
nodes.notes: Students and instructors uploading academic papers directly or via integrations.

nodes.name: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)
nodes.notes: SNS topic triggered when a paper is uploaded and ready for processing.

nodes.name: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)
nodes.notes: SQS queue buffering up to 2 million incoming paper messages per day.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Orchestrator)
nodes.notes: Java-based orchestrator and rules engine determining paper processing eligibility.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Processing)
nodes.notes: Python-based processing Lambda breaking down prose text into sentence sliding windows.

nodes.name: Amazon SageMaker
nodes.notes: SageMaker endpoint running on EC2 for high-concurrency generative AI inference.

nodes.name: Amazon DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores document and sentence-level AI evaluation scores.

nodes.name: MFE
nodes.notes: Micro Front End web component embedded into existing user-facing applications.

edges.notes: User uploads paper to platform, triggering an SNS notification topic.
SNS pushes paper upload event to the SQS queue.
Orchestrator Lambda polls SQS queue and applies filtering rules.
Orchestrator Lambda invokes Processing Lambda for sentence segmentation.
Processing Lambda sends sentence sliding windows in parallel to SageMaker endpoint.
SageMaker returns AI sentence inference results back to Processing Lambda.
Processing Lambda returns aggregated document and sentence scores to Orchestrator Lambda.
Orchestrator Lambda persists sentence and paper score records into DynamoDB.
Micro Front End component queries Orchestrator Lambda to retrieve paper score details.
DynamoDB returns paper analysis records to Orchestrator Lambda to display in MFE.
